data.title: Pitted keratolysis — viva
data.summary: Bacterial infections · 6 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Pitted keratolysis** (Bacterial infections)_

**Q1. What is pitted keratolysis and what causes it?**
- Superficial infection of the stratum corneum of soles (keratoma plantare sulcatum, ringed keratolysis)
- Kytococcus sedentarius (main), Dermatophilus congolensis, Corynebacterium, Actinomyces — produce keratin-degrading proteases

**Q2. Clinical features?**
- Multiple 1–7 mm crateriform pits, coalescing into furrows, on pressure-bearing areas of soles (heel, ball, toe pads); worse when wet
- Hyperhidrosis and malodour (sulfur compounds — thiols, thioesters) are characteristic; sliminess; asymptomatic or sore

**Q3. Predisposing factors?**
- Hyperhidrosis, occlusive footwear (soldiers, athletes, farmers), hot humid climate, barefoot walking in wet conditions

**Q4. Diagnosis?**
- Clinical; dermoscopy shows pits with visible walls; Wood's lamp — coral-red fluorescence may be seen (corynebacteria)
- Histopathology: pits in stratum corneum with Gram-positive coccobacilli/filaments on PAS/Gram stain

**Q5. Differential diagnosis?**
- Tinea pedis, plantar warts, punctate palmoplantar keratoderma, basal cell naevus syndrome pits, arsenical keratoses, callosities

**Q6. Treatment and prevention?**
- Topical erythromycin/clindamycin/fusidic acid/mupirocin, benzoyl peroxide wash, topical azoles; treat hyperhidrosis (aluminium chloride, iontophoresis, botulinum toxin)
- Prevention: dry feet, absorbent cotton socks changed often, breathable shoes, antiperspirants

## Quick spotter facts
- Crater-like pits on the sole with foul smell — pitted keratolysis

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Bacterial infections — pitted keratolysis); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.15. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
